topics.title: Meaning of Ethnicity: Problems of Ethnicity in Nigeria and Ethnic Groups in Nigeria | Primary 4 (Basic 4) Third Term Week 2 Civic Education
topics.content:
MEANING OF ETHNICITY: PROBLEMS OF ETHNICITY IN NIGERIA AND ETHNIC GROUPS IN NIGERIA
CIVIC EDUCATION
PRIMARY 4 - THIRD TERM - WEEK 2
THEME - NATIONAL VALUES EDUCATION
PREVIOUS LESSON - Duties and Responsibilities of Parents and Children in Building the Nation | Primary 4 (Basic 4) Second Term Week 10 Civic Education
TOPIC - ETHNICITY
LEARNING
1. Introduction
2. Meaning and Examples of Ethnicity in Nigeria
3. Problems of Ethnicity in Nigeria
4. How to promote Unity among Ethnicity
5. Weekly Assessment: Test Questions and Answers/Assignment
6. Summary
LEARNING OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:
1. Explain the meaning of ethnicity.
2. Mention at least five ethnic groups in Nigeria.
3. Identify some ethnic groups and where they are mainly found.
4. Mention at least five problems of ethnicity in Nigeria.
5. Explain how ethnicity can affect peace and unity.
6. State ways of promoting unity among different ethnic groups.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
Pupils have previously learned about Nigerian culture, people, and communities.
This lesson builds on that knowledge by teaching pupils about ethnicity, ethnic groups in Nigeria, the problems of ethnicity, and ways of promoting unity.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
1. Map of Nigeria
2. Pictures of different Nigerian cultural groups
3. Pictures of traditional clothing
4. Pictures of cultural festivals
5. Flashcards
6. Charts showing ethnic groups
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Scheme of Work
2. 9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
3. Course Book
4. All Relevant Material
5. Online Information
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
INTRODUCTION
Nigeria is a country with many ethnic groups. These groups have different languages, cultures, traditions, and ways of life.
People from different ethnic groups live and work together across Nigeria. However, treating people unfairly because of their ethnic group can cause problems such as discrimination, conflict, and division.
In this lesson, pupils will learn about the meaning of ethnicity, ethnic groups in Nigeria, problems of ethnicity, and ways of promoting peace and unity among Nigerians.
LESSON 1 - MEANING OF ETHNICITY
Ethnicity means the identity of a group of people who share things such as language, culture, traditions, history, or ancestry.
Nigeria has many ethnic groups with different languages and cultures.
Examples of Ethnic Groups in Nigeria
Some major ethnic groups in Nigeria include:
1. Yoruba - An ethnic group mainly found in south-western Nigeria.
2. Hausa - An ethnic group mainly found in northern Nigeria.
3. Igbo - An ethnic group mainly found in south-eastern Nigeria.
4. Ijaw - An ethnic group mainly found in the Niger Delta region.
5. Kanuri - An ethnic group mainly found in north-eastern Nigeria.
6. Tiv - An ethnic group mainly found in Benue and nearby areas.
7. Edo - An ethnic group mainly found in Edo State.
8. Ibibio - An ethnic group mainly found in Akwa Ibom State.
9. Efik - An ethnic group mainly found in Cross River State.
10. Urhobo - An ethnic group mainly found in Delta State.
Every ethnic group has its own culture, language, traditions, and way of life.
LESSON 2 - PROBLEMS OF ETHNICITY IN NIGERIA
Ethnicity can become a problem when people treat members of other ethnic groups unfairly.
Some problems include:
1. Discrimination - treating people unfairly because of their ethnic group.
2. Ethnic conflict - fighting between different ethnic groups.
3. Lack of unity - people may put their ethnic group before the country.
4. Stereotyping - having unfair ideas about another ethnic group.
5. Nepotism - giving unfair preference to people from one’s own group.
6. Political division - ethnicity can sometimes cause disagreements in politics.
7. Hate and mistrust - people may dislike or distrust people from other groups.
LESSON 3 - HOW TO PROMOTE UNITY AMONG ETHNIC GROUPS
We can promote peace and unity by:
1. Respecting other ethnic groups.
2. Learning about other people’s cultures.
3. Avoiding discrimination.
4. Treating everyone fairly.
5. Working together.
6. Living peacefully with others.
7. Promoting love and friendship.
8. Putting Nigeria’s interest first.
WEEKLY ASSESSMENT: TEST QUESTIONS AND ANSWERS/ASSIGNMENT
A. Multiple Choice Questions
1. Ethnicity refers to the identity of a group of people who share common ______.
A. culture and language
B. food only
C. houses
D. vehicles
2. Which of the following is an ethnic group in Nigeria?
A. Hospital
B. School
C. Yoruba
D. Market
3. The Hausa are mainly found in ______ Nigeria.
A. southern
B. northern
C. western
D. coastal
4. Which of the following is a problem of ethnicity?
A. Unity
B. Cooperation
C. Friendship
D. Discrimination
5. Which action promotes unity among ethnic groups?
A. Fighting other groups
B. Respecting other ethnic groups
C. Discriminating against others
D. Insulting other cultures
B. Fill in the Gaps
Use the following words to complete the sentences: Unity, ethnicity, discrimination, Yoruba, Igbo
6. ______ is the identity of a group of people who share common culture and traditions.
7. The ______ are mainly found in south-western Nigeria.
8. The ______ are mainly found in south-eastern Nigeria.
9. Treating people unfairly because of their ethnic group is called ______.
10. Respect and cooperation help to promote ______ among Nigerians.
C. True or False
11. Nigeria has many ethnic groups. ______
12. Yoruba, Hausa, and Igbo are examples of ethnic groups in Nigeria. ______
13. Discrimination can cause problems among ethnic groups. ______
14. People should hate other ethnic groups because they have different cultures. ______
15. Respecting other ethnic groups promotes peace and unity. ______
D. Matching
16. Yoruba - A. Mainly found in northern Nigeria
17. Hausa - B. Mainly found in south-eastern Nigeria
18. Igbo - C. Identity based on shared culture, language, or traditions
19. Kanuri - D. Mainly found in south-western Nigeria
20. Ethnicity - E. Mainly found in north-eastern Nigeria
ANSWER KEYS
1. A 2. C 3. B 4. D 5. B
6. ethnicity
7. Yoruba
8. Igbo
9. discrimination
10. unity
11. True
12. True
13. True
14. False
15. True
16. Yoruba - D. Mainly found in south-western Nigeria
17. Hausa - A. Mainly found in northern Nigeria
18. Igbo - B. Mainly found in south-eastern Nigeria
19. Kanuri - E. Mainly found in north-eastern Nigeria
20. Ethnicity - C. Identity based on shared culture, language, or traditions
SUMMARY
In this lesson, pupils learned that ethnicity is the identity of a group of people who share common culture, language, traditions, history, or ancestry.
They learned about some ethnic groups in Nigeria, such as Yoruba, Hausa, Igbo, Ijaw, Kanuri, Tiv, Edo, Ibibio, Efik, and Urhobo.
Pupils also learned that problems of ethnicity include discrimination, ethnic conflict, lack of unity, stereotyping, and mistrust. They learned that respect, fairness, cooperation, and peaceful living can promote unity among different ethnic groups.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
Step 1: Introduction
The teacher displays pictures of people from different Nigerian ethnic groups and a map of Nigeria.
The teacher asks:
- What differences can you see among the people?
- Do all Nigerians speak the same language?
- Can people from different ethnic groups live together peacefully?
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils observe the pictures and answer the questions.
Step 2: Meaning of Ethnicity
The teacher explains that ethnicity is the identity of a group of people who share common culture, language, traditions, history, or ancestry.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils listen and explain the meaning of ethnicity in their own words.
Step 3: Ethnic Groups in Nigeria
The teacher explains that Nigeria has many ethnic groups, including:
- Yoruba - Mainly found in south-western Nigeria.
- Hausa - Mainly found in northern Nigeria.
- Igbo - Mainly found in south-eastern Nigeria.
- Ijaw - Mainly found in the Niger Delta region.
- Kanuri - Mainly found in north-eastern Nigeria.
- Tiv - Mainly found in Benue and nearby areas.
- Edo - Mainly found in Edo State.
- Ibibio - Mainly found in Akwa Ibom State.
- Efik - Mainly found in Cross River State.
- Urhobo - Mainly found in Delta State.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils identify the ethnic groups and locate some of them on the map.
Step 4: Problems of Ethnicity
The teacher explains that ethnicity can become a problem when people treat others unfairly because of their ethnic group.
Problems include:
- Discrimination - Treating people unfairly because of their ethnic group.
- Ethnic conflict - Fighting between different ethnic groups.
- Lack of unity - People may put their ethnic group before the country.
- Stereotyping - Having unfair ideas about another ethnic group.
- Mistrust - Lack of trust between different groups.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils mention some problems that can arise from ethnic differences.
Step 5: Promoting Unity
The teacher explains that Nigerians can promote unity by:
- Respecting other ethnic groups.
- Treating everyone fairly.
- Learning about other cultures.
- Working together.
- Avoiding discrimination.
- Living peacefully with others.
- Showing love and friendship.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils state ways they can promote unity in their school and community.
Step 6: Group Activity
The teacher divides the pupils into groups:
- Group 1: List five ethnic groups in Nigeria.
- Group 2: State five problems of ethnicity.
- Group 3: State five ways of promoting unity.
- Group 4: Match some ethnic groups with the areas where they are mainly found.
Each group presents its work to the class.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils discuss, write, and present their answers.
Step 7: Lesson Summary
The teacher reviews the meaning of ethnicity, ethnic groups in Nigeria, problems of ethnicity, and ways of promoting unity.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils answer oral questions and summarise the lesson.
Step 8: Evaluation
The teacher gives pupils the practice exercise.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils complete the Multiple Choice, Fill in the Gaps, True or False, and Matching questions.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
NEXT LESSON
Causes of Ethnicity: Economic, Political and Tribal Causes of Ethnicity in Nigeria | Primary 4 (Basic 4) Third Term Week 3 Civic Education
LESSON EVALUATION
Teacher asks pupils to,
1. Explain the meaning of ethnicity.
2. Mention at least five ethnic groups in Nigeria.
3. State where some ethnic groups are mainly found.
4. Mention at least four problems of ethnicity.
5. Explain how discrimination can cause problems among ethnic groups.
6. State at least four ways of promoting unity among ethnic groups in Nigeria.

CAUSES OF ETHNICITY: ECONOMIC, POLITICAL AND TRIBAL CAUSES OF ETHNICITY IN NIGERIA
CIVIC EDUCATION
PRIMARY 4 - THIRD TERM - WEEK 3
THEME - NATIONAL VALUES EDUCATION
PREVIOUS LESSON - Meaning of Ethnicity: Problems of Ethnicity in Nigeria and Ethnic Groups in Nigeria | Primary 4 (Basic 4) Third Term Week 2 Civic Education
TOPIC - CAUSES OF ETHNICITY
LEARNING
1. Introduction
2. Meaning of Causes of Ethnicity
3. Economic, Political and Tribal Causes
4. Effects of Ethnicity and Ways to Reduce Ethnic Division in Nigeria
5. Weekly Assessment: Test Questions and Answers/Assignment
6. Summary
LEARNING OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:
1. Explain the meaning of causes of ethnicity.
2. Mention at least three economic causes of ethnicity.
3. Mention at least three political causes of ethnicity.
4. Mention at least three tribal causes of ethnicity.
5. Explain how economic and political competition can cause ethnic division.
6. State ways of reducing ethnic division in Nigeria.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
Pupils have previously learned about the meaning of ethnicity, ethnic groups in Nigeria, and problems of ethnicity.
This lesson builds on that knowledge by teaching pupils about the economic, political, and tribal causes of ethnicity in Nigeria.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
1. Map of Nigeria
2. Pictures of different ethnic groups
3. Pictures of Nigerian cultural activities
4. Flashcards
5. Charts showing causes of ethnicity
6. Pictures showing people working together
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.

CONTENT OF THE LESSON
INTRODUCTION
Nigeria has many ethnic groups with different languages, cultures, and traditions. These differences make Nigeria a diverse country.
Sometimes, economic problems, political competition, and tribal differences can make people favour their own ethnic groups or create division among people.
In this lesson, pupils will learn about the economic, political, and tribal causes of ethnicity in Nigeria and ways of promoting unity among different ethnic groups.
LESSON 1 - MEANING OF CAUSES OF ETHNICITY
Causes of ethnicity are the reasons why people may identify strongly with their ethnic group or allow ethnic differences to create division.
ECONOMIC CAUSES OF ETHNICITY
Economic problems can increase ethnic divisions when people feel that their ethnic group is not getting enough opportunities or resources.
Examples include:
1. Unequal sharing of resources - Some people may feel that resources are not shared fairly.
2. Unemployment - Lack of jobs can cause competition among groups.
3. Poverty - Poor living conditions can increase competition for opportunities.
4. Competition for opportunities - People may compete for jobs, education, and other benefits.
Political Causes of Ethnicity
Politics can sometimes increase ethnic differences when people support leaders mainly because they belong to their ethnic group.
Examples include:
1. Ethnic political support - Supporting a candidate mainly because of their ethnic group.
2. Political competition - Groups may compete for political power.
3. Unequal political opportunities - Some groups may feel left out of political positions.
4. Political favouritism - Giving unfair advantages to members of a particular group.
LESSON 2 - TRIBAL CAUSES OF ETHNICITY
Tribal causes are linked to strong attachment to one’s ethnic group and differences between groups.
Examples include:
1. Language differences - Different languages can sometimes create barriers.
2. Cultural differences - Different customs and traditions may cause misunderstanding.
3. Prejudice - Having negative ideas about another ethnic group.
4. Discrimination - Treating people unfairly because of their ethnic group.
5. Lack of understanding - Not knowing or respecting other people’s cultures.
EFFECTS OF ETHNIC DIVISION
When ethnic differences are badly handled, they can lead to:
1. Discrimination.
2. Conflict and violence.
3. Lack of unity.
4. Mistrust.
5. Political division.
6. Slow national development.
LESSON 3 - WAYS TO REDUCE ETHNIC DIVISION
We can reduce ethnic division by:
1. Treating everyone fairly.
2. Respecting different cultures.
3. Promoting equal opportunities.
4. Working together.
5. Avoiding discrimination.
6. Supporting peaceful dialogue.
7. Putting national interest above ethnic interest.
WEEKLY ASSESSMENT: TEST QUESTIONS AND ANSWERS/ASSIGNMENT
A. Multiple Choice Questions
1. One cause of ethnicity in Nigeria is ______.
A. friendship
B. unity
C. cooperation
D. unfair treatment
2. Which of the following is an economic cause of ethnicity?
A. Respect for others
B. Competition for jobs
C. National unity
D. Helping neighbours
3. Which of the following is a political cause of ethnicity?
A. Peace
B. Hard work
C. Cooperation
D. Political favouritism
4. Which of the following is a tribal cause of ethnicity?
A. Teamwork
B. Equal treatment
C. Cultural differences
D. Friendship
5. Which of the following can help reduce ethnic division?
A. Respecting other cultures
B. Discrimination
C. Fighting
D. Tribal hatred
B. Fill in the Gaps
Use the following below to complete the sentences: jobs, culture, political, unity, discrimination
6. Competition for ______ can cause ethnic division.
7. ______ competition can increase ethnic differences.
8. Different traditions and ______ may sometimes cause misunderstanding.
9. Treating people unfairly because of their ethnic group is called ______.
10. Respect and cooperation promote national ______.
C. True or False
11. Employment can contribute to ethnic division. ______
12. Political favouritism can reduce ethnic tension. ______
13. Cultural differences always cause conflict. ______
14. Discrimination can increase ethnic division. ______
15. Respecting other cultures can promote unity. ______
D. Matching
16. Competition for jobs - A. Tribal cause
17. Political favouritism - B. Promotes unity
18. Cultural differences - C. Economic cause
19. Discrimination - D. Political cause
20. Respect for other cultures - E. Can increase ethnic division
ANSWER KEYS
1. D 2. B 3. D 4. C 5. A
6. jobs
7. political
8. culture
9. discrimination
10. unity
11. False
12. False
13. False
14. True
15. True
16. Competition for jobs - C. Economic cause
17. Political favouritism - D. Political cause
18. Cultural differences - A. Tribal cause
19. Discrimination - E. Can increase ethnic division
20. Respect for other cultures - B. Promotes unity
SUMMARY
In this lesson, pupils learned that ethnicity can be caused by economic, political, and tribal factors.
They learned that economic causes include competition for jobs, unemployment, poverty, and competition for resources. Political causes include political favouritism and competition for political power. Tribal causes include cultural differences, language differences, prejudice, and discrimination.
Pupils also learned that fairness, respect, cooperation, and equal opportunities can help reduce ethnic division and promote unity in Nigeria.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
Step 1: Introduction
The teacher displays pictures showing different ethnic groups, people competing for jobs, political activities, and cultural activities.
The teacher asks:
- Why do people sometimes favour their ethnic group?
- Can competition for jobs cause disagreement?
- Can cultural differences cause misunderstanding?
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils observe the pictures and answer the questions.
Step 2: Meaning of Causes of Ethnicity
The teacher explains that causes of ethnicity are the reasons why people may favour their ethnic group or allow ethnic differences to create division.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils listen and explain the meaning in their own words.
Step 3: Economic Causes
The teacher explains that economic problems can cause ethnic division.
Examples include:
- Competition for jobs.
- Unemployment.
- Poverty.
- Competition for resources and opportunities.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils mention some economic causes of ethnicity.
Step 4: Political Causes
The teacher explains that political activities can sometimes increase ethnic differences.
Examples include:
- Political favouritism.
- Competition for political power.
- Unequal political opportunities.
- Supporting leaders mainly because of their ethnic group.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils mention some political causes of ethnicity.
Step 5: Tribal Causes
The teacher explains that strong attachment to one’s ethnic group can also cause division.
Examples include:
- Cultural differences.
- Language differences.
- Prejudice.
- Discrimination.
- Lack of understanding of other cultures.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils identify some tribal causes of ethnicity.
Step 6: Ways to Reduce Ethnic Division
The teacher explains that ethnic division can be reduced by:
- Respecting other cultures.
- Treating everyone fairly.
- Providing equal opportunities.
- Working together.
- Avoiding discrimination.
- Promoting peace and unity.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils state ways they can promote unity in their school and community.
Step 7: Group Activity
The teacher divides the pupils into groups:
- Group 1: List five economic causes of ethnicity.
- Group 2: List four political causes of ethnicity.
- Group 3: List five tribal causes of ethnicity.
- Group 4: List five ways of reducing ethnic division.
Each group presents its work to the class.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils discuss, write, and present their answers.
Step 8: Lesson Summary
The teacher reviews the economic, political, and tribal causes of ethnicity and ways of reducing ethnic division.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils answer oral questions and summarise the lesson.
Step 9: Evaluation
The teacher gives pupils the practice exercise.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils complete the Multiple Choice, Fill in the Gaps, True or False, and Matching questions.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.

CONTENT OF THE LESSON
INTRODUCTION
Nigeria has many ethnic groups with different languages, cultures, and traditions. These differences can enrich the country when people respect one another.
However, when people allow ethnic differences to cause hatred, discrimination, or division, they can create serious problems. These problems may include communal conflicts, political violence, and nepotism.
In this lesson, pupils will learn about the consequences of ethnicity and ways of promoting peace, fairness, and unity in Nigeria.
LESSON 1 AND LESSON 2 - MEANING OF CONSEQUENCES OF ETHNICITY
Consequences of ethnicity are the problems that can happen when people allow ethnic differences to cause division, hatred, or unfair treatment.
CONSEQUENCES OF ETHNICITY
1. Communal Conflicts
Communal conflict is a disagreement or fight between groups of people living in a community.
Ethnic differences can sometimes lead to conflicts between communities.
Examples of effects include:
- Fighting between groups.
- Destruction of property.
- Loss of lives.
- People leaving their homes.
- Fear and insecurity.
2. Political Violence
Political violence is the use of force or fighting during political activities.
Ethnicity can sometimes cause political violence when people support or oppose others because of their ethnic group.
Examples include:
- Fighting during political activities.
- Destruction of property.
- Injuries and loss of lives.
- Fear among citizens.
- Disruption of peace.
3. Nepotism
Nepotism means giving unfair favour or opportunities to relatives or members of one’s own group.
For example, a person in a position of authority may give a job or benefit to someone because they belong to the same ethnic group instead of choosing the most qualified person.
Nepotism can lead to:
- Unfair treatment.
- Lack of equal opportunities.
- Poor leadership.
- Lack of trust.
- Division among people.
LESSON 3 - OTHER CONSEQUENCES OF ETHNICITY
Other consequences may include:
4. Discrimination - Treating people unfairly because of their ethnic group.
5. Lack of unity - People may put ethnic interests above national interests.
6. Mistrust - People may lose trust in members of other ethnic groups.
7. Slow development - Conflict and division can affect national development.
8. Insecurity - Ethnic conflicts can make communities unsafe.
WAYS TO REDUCE THE CONSEQUENCES OF ETHNICITY
We can reduce these problems by:

2. Treating everyone fairly.
3. Avoiding discrimination.
4. Promoting equal opportunities.
5. Working together peacefully.
6. Rejecting nepotism.

SUMMARY
In this lesson, pupils learned that consequences of ethnicity are the problems that can result when ethnic differences cause division or unfair treatment.
They learned about communal conflict, political violence, and nepotism. They also learned that ethnicity can lead to discrimination, mistrust, insecurity, and lack of unity.
Pupils learned that respect, fairness, equal treatment, cooperation, and peaceful living can help reduce the negative effects of ethnicity.

Step 1: Introduction
The teacher displays pictures showing different ethnic groups, community conflicts, political activities, and people working together.
The teacher asks:

- Lack of trust.

Step 6: Other Consequences of Ethnicity

CONTENT OF THE LESSON
INTRODUCTION
Nigeria is made up of many ethnic groups with different languages, cultures, and traditions. These differences should not stop Nigerians from living together peacefully.
Problems such as discrimination, conflict, nepotism, and political violence can divide people. However, these problems can be reduced when people respect one another, treat everyone fairly, and work together.
In this lesson, pupils will learn about ways of solving the problems of ethnicity and promoting peace, unity, and cooperation among Nigerians.
LESSON 1 - MEANING OF SOLUTIONS TO ETHNICITY
Solutions to ethnicity are the ways of reducing ethnic problems and promoting peace, unity, and cooperation among different ethnic groups.
WAYS OF SOLVING THE PROBLEMS OF ETHNICITY
1. Respect for all ethnic groups - We should respect people from different ethnic groups.
2. Equal treatment - Everyone should be treated fairly, regardless of their ethnic group.
3. Avoid discrimination - People should not be treated badly because of their ethnic group.
4. Promote unity - Nigerians should work together as one people.
5. Respect different cultures - We should respect the languages, traditions, and cultures of other groups.
6. Equal opportunities - Jobs, education, and other opportunities should be given fairly.
7. Peaceful dialogue - People should settle disagreements through discussion instead of fighting.
8. Avoid Nepotism - Leaders should not give unfair advantages to relatives or members of their ethnic group.
9. Encourage inter-ethnic friendship - People from different ethnic groups should live and work together peacefully.
10. Promote national unity - Nigerians should put the interest of Nigeria above ethnic interests.
LESSON 2 - ROLE OF PUPILS IN PROMOTING UNITY
Pupils can help by:
1. Respecting classmates from different ethnic groups.
2. Avoiding ethnic insults.
3. Playing and working with everyone.
4. Learning about other cultures.
5. Treating everyone fairly.
6. Reporting bullying and discrimination to a trusted adult.

In this lesson, pupils learned that solutions to ethnicity are ways of reducing ethnic problems and promoting peace and unity.
They learned that ethnic problems can be reduced by:
- Respecting other ethnic groups.
- Treating everyone fairly.
- Avoiding discrimination.
- Giving equal opportunities.
- Promoting peaceful dialogue.
- Working together.
- Avoiding nepotism.
- Promoting national unity.

The teacher displays pictures of different ethnic groups, people working together, and peaceful community activities.

People from different ethnic groups live together in many Nigerian communities. Sometimes, disagreements may occur among them.
A community leader is a person who leads and guides people in a community. Community leaders help people to settle disagreements, promote peace, encourage unity, and work together.
In this lesson, pupils will learn about the duties of community leaders in ensuring peaceful co-existence between different ethnic groups.
LESSON 1 AND LESSON 2 - DUTIES OF COMMUNITY LEADERS IN ENSURING PEACEFUL CO-EXISTENCE BETWEEN ETHNIC GROUPS
A person who leads and guides people in a community.
Community leaders play an important role in helping people from different ethnic groups live together peacefully.

6. Explain the importance of respecting other ethnic groups.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
Pupils have previously learned about ethnicity, its causes and consequences, and ways of solving ethnic problems.
This lesson builds on that knowledge by teaching pupils about the meaning of identity, ethnicity, and tribalism and how tribalism can affect peaceful co-existence.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS

2. Pictures showing different Nigerian cultures
3. Map of Nigeria

CONTENT OF THE LESSON
INTRODUCTION
Every person has an identity that helps others know who they are. People may have different languages, cultures, traditions, and backgrounds.
Ethnicity describes the shared identity of a group, while tribalism occurs when people unfairly favour their own ethnic group over others.
In this lesson, pupils will learn the meaning of identity, ethnicity, and tribalism, as well as the importance of treating people from all ethnic groups fairly.
LESSON 1 - MEANING OF IDENTITY
Identity is the way a person or group is known by their name, culture, language, traditions, or background.
For example, a person may identify with a particular ethnic group because of their language, culture, or family background.
MEANING OF TRIBALISM
Tribalism is showing strong support or favour towards one’s own ethnic or tribal group, sometimes at the expense of other groups.
For example, choosing someone for a job only because they belong to the same ethnic group is an example of tribalism.
MEANING OF ETHNICITY
Ethnicity is the identity of a group of people who share common culture, language, traditions, history, or ancestry.
DIFFERENCE BETWEEN ETHNICITY AND TRIBALISM
1. Ethnicity describes the identity and shared background of a group.

CONTENT OF THE LESSON
INTRODUCTION
Nigeria has many ethnic groups with different languages, cultures, and traditions. These differences are part of Nigeria’s diversity.
Ethnicity describes the shared identity of a group, while tribalism involves unfair favour towards one’s own ethnic group. When people refuse to respect or accept people from other ethnic groups, it can lead to tribal intolerance.
In this lesson, pupils will learn about the similarities and differences between ethnicity and tribalism, tribal intolerance, and ways of promoting tolerance and unity.
LESSON 1 - MEANING OF ETHNICITY
Ethnicity is the identity of a group of people who share common culture, language, traditions, history, or background.
MEANING OF TRIBALISM
Tribalism is unfair favour towards one’s own ethnic group, especially when a person treats other groups unfairly.
SIMILARITIES BETWEEN ETHNICITY AND TRIBALISM
Ethnicity and tribalism are related because:
1. Both are connected to ethnic groups.
2. Both involve people’s culture, language, and traditions.
3. Both can influence how people identify with a group.
4. Both can affect relationships between different groups.

DIFFERENCES BETWEEN ETHNICITY AND TRIBALISM
1. Ethnicity describes the shared identity and background of a group.
2. Tribalism is the unfair preference or support of one’s own ethnic group.
3. Ethnicity is not necessarily harmful.
4. Tribalism can lead to discrimination and division.
LESSON 2 - MEANING OF TRIBAL INTOLERANCE
Tribal intolerance means refusing to accept, respect, or live peacefully with people from other ethnic groups.
For example, insulting someone or refusing to work with them simply because they belong to another ethnic group is tribal intolerance.
EFFECTS OF TRIBAL INTOLERANCE
Tribal intolerance can lead to:
1. Discrimination
2. Hatred
3. Communal conflicts
4. Lack of unity
5. Mistrust
6. Political violence
8. Slow national development

4. Learning about other cultures

They also learned that tribalism means unfair favour towards one’s own ethnic group. Tribal intolerance means refusing to respect or accept people from other ethnic groups.
Pupils learned that tribal intolerance can cause discrimination, hatred, conflict, mistrust, and lack of unity. They also learned that respect, tolerance, fairness, cooperation, and equal treatment can help promote peaceful co-existence.
